title: The boundary of a dense affine open has pure codimension one
statement: Let $X$ be a separated locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every irreducible component $Z$ of the closed subset $|X|\setminus|U|$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] and every generic point $\xi$ of $Z$ [def-sc-generic-point], the local ring of $X$ at $\xi$ satisfies $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Here dense means $\overline{|U|}=|X|$. If $U=X$, there are no such components and the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0BCV, divisors-lemma-complement-affine-open; the dense-open clause. Used in the proof of Tag 0BCW, divisors-lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor.

proof.text: Fix a boundary component $Z$ and its generic point $\xi$. Write $F=|X|\setminus|U|$. The open immersion $j:U\to X$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism]: its source is affine and its target is separated. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $\xi$ from the scheme charts [def-pc-scheme]. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Set $A=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $R$ corresponding to $\xi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$; hence $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. It is a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0BCV, lemma-complement-affine-open; Tag 0BCU, lemma-complement-affine-open-immersion, local reduction; Tag 01SG, affine permanence

proof.text: Let $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ be the canonical local-spectrum morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. Its image is the generalizations of $\xi$, and $c(\mathfrak m)=\xi$. On $V$ it is the localization map $\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathfrak p}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, which is a topological embedding by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding]. If $y$ generalizes $\xi$ and $y\in F$, then $\overline{\{y\}}$ is an irreducible closed subset of $F$ containing $\overline{\{\xi\}}=Z$. Maximality of the component $Z$ forces equality. Uniqueness of its generic point [lem-sc-scheme-sober] then gives $y=\xi$. Conversely $\xi\in F$. Injectivity of $c$ therefore proves $c^{-1}(F)=\{\mathfrak m\}$. Thus the open pullback $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A=c^{-1}(U)$ is exactly the punctured open subscheme $P=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$; both have the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0BCU, lemma-complement-affine-open-immersion, first paragraph; Tag 01J7, lemma-specialize-points

proof.text: The projection $P=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine by base change of $j$, using clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Its target is affine, so clause (2) makes $P$ affine. The local ring $A$ is Noetherian by Step 1; applying [lem-sfb-affine-punctured-local-dimension] now gives $\dim A\leq1$.

source.place: Tags 0BCU and 0BCR; Tag 01SD, base change of affine morphisms

proof.text: It remains to rule out dimension zero. The affine neighbourhood $V$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ covering it; [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives their generic points $\eta_i$. Each $C_i$ meets the dense open $U\cap V$: indeed $W_i=V\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne i}C_h$ is a nonempty open subset contained in $C_i$. It is nonempty because otherwise irreducibility and the finite union would put $C_i$ inside some other component, contrary to maximality. Density makes $W_i\cap U$ nonempty. Since every nonempty relatively open subset of $C_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$ contains $\eta_i$, it follows that $\eta_i\in U$. Choose a component containing $\xi$. Its generic point $\eta_i$ strictly generalizes $\xi$, since $\xi\notin U$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] this length-one chain implies $1\leq\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$. Combined with Step 3 this gives the required equality. If the boundary is empty, there is no choice of $Z$ and the assertion is vacuous.
